questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “Testing Reactive Forms”?
options: Testing Reactive Forms means the browser can enforce all permissions without the backend.
Testing Reactive Forms removes the need for error handling, accessibility checks and tests.
Testing Reactive Forms should be implemented by copying a snippet without checking the Angular version.

questions.answer_key: Testing Reactive Forms helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.

questions.prompt: How should a learner work with “Testing validators” in this lesson?
options: Assume “Testing validators” works identically across every Angular major and runtime.
Use “Testing validators” to bypass runtime validation of external or user-provided values.
Connect “Testing validators” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
Treat “Testing validators” as a reason to skip the surrounding application context.
questions.answer_key: Connect “Testing validators” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.explanation: The PDF explicitly lists “Testing validators” under Testing Reactive Forms. Anchor it in a small example and check the behavior rather than relying on a memorized phrase.

questions.prompt: What is the strongest verification approach for “Testing Reactive Forms”?
options: Ignore a failing test if the component looks correct in one browser.
Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
Assume an SVG diagram proves the code compiled and passed tests.
Treat a successful client-side render as backend authorization evidence.
questions.answer_key: Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
questions.explanation: Verification evidence should match the running environment. Static teaching snippets are not compiler output, and frontend checks do not replace backend authorization.
